Credit: luch91's query-key change and yukkie3276's earlier CORS/cache finding (PR754 comment6073595328); this extends known evidence, not a new discovery. Pinned main0e47f770b13cc27e1e2e199d4cdf70a4778c97cc and PRhead8cf6d7d71df4b62ef1c6ba99c659a440f24f6c97, open/unmerged at check. Windows native Node full Worker module with generated snapshot routing and real fetch to local Starlette CORSMiddleware/Uvicorn: 16 scenarios/version, main15/16, PR8/16, companion proposal16/16; 83 actual health HTTP requests across48 scenarios. Main's mismatch is desired query collapse; eight PR mismatches are request-order manifestations of one previously reported header/key gap. The cache is a Vary-aware in-memory substitute, NOT a Cloudflare deployment test or actual browser CORS enforcement. Two allowed sites, denied/empty/absent Origin, Korean query variants, HEAD, OPTIONS, POST405 and uncached503 are covered. A headerless canonical cache Request can return another caller's CORS header. Companion patch skips shared cache reads/writes for Origin-bearing GETs and sets no-store, while retaining origin-free query collapse/caching and canonical upstream URLs. Tradeoff: every Origin-bearing GET reaches origin (32 vs20 health requests in this fixture). 12 source Git blobs and executed checker/source hashes verified; patch apply check, syntax and Python checker Ruff pass. No full upstream Linux CI, real cache TTL/eviction/isolate tests, production incident or private-data leak is claimed. User key was not used in tests; it is used internally only for this authorized signature/delivery.
